script.title: Ohio State refused Michigan's forfeit in a 1950 blizzard 😱
sentences: Dick Larkins said no to a Michigan forfeit.
This was Ohio State against Michigan in Columbus, November 25, 1950.
It was 10 degrees, and snow was falling two inches an hour.
Both coaches wanted out, and a cancelled game would have left Ohio State Big Ten champion.
Larkins, Ohio State's athletic director, made them play anyway.
Fans lit small bonfires in the stands, and the two teams punted 45 times.
Michigan never made a single first down.
They won 9 to 3, and every point came off a blocked punt.
Ohio State's coach resigned 18 days later.
script.description:
Before this weekend's Ohio State vs Michigan, meet the Snow Bowl.
November 25, 1950, Columbus.
claims_en: Ohio State athletic director Dick Larkins would not accept Michigan's forfeit
The game was Michigan vs Ohio State in Columbus (Ohio Stadium) on November 25, 1950
The temperature was 10 degrees and snow fell at two inches per hour
Neither coach (Fesler nor Oosterbaan) wanted to play the game
If the game had not been played, Ohio State would have been Big Ten champion
Larkins would not accept the forfeit and the game proceeded
Some fans built small bonfires in the stands to keep warm
Michigan never got a first down
Michigan won 9-3; its points came from a safety on a blocked punt and a touchdown recovered on a blocked punt plus the extra point
Ohio State coach Wes Fesler submitted his resignation 18 days later
scenes: Extreme close-up of a stern 1950s American college athletic director in a snow-dusted fedora and overcoat, jaw set, eyes defiant, snowflakes whirling, grey blizzard light
Wide shot of a huge horseshoe-shaped 1950 college stadium buried in a blizzard, crowds in heavy coats, snow swirling under a dark grey sky
Close shot of a frozen football field with snow piling up, yard lines vanished, goalposts barely visible through heavy falling snow
Two worried 1950s football coaches in long overcoats arguing with two officials in a cramped stadium office, frost on the window, tense faces
The athletic director standing firm with folded arms as others look at him in disbelief, snow blowing past the doorway, medium shot
Fans in 1950s coats huddled around small bonfires in snowy stadium stands, some with cardboard boxes over their heads, orange firelight against blue snow
Players in leather helmets and wool uniforms slipping in deep snow, the ball spinning loose, blizzard haze, low angle
A player in a 1950s maize and blue uniform diving to block a punt in the snow, the ball deflecting off his arms, dramatic freeze frame
A lone 1950s coach in an overcoat walking out of an empty snowy stadium at dusk, head down, long shadow
